quotes.text: A label with no enforced policy is a sticker. A scope with no allow list is an invitation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisp warning that labels and scopes only protect when they are enforced.

quotes.text: If your tenant has everyone except external libraries with HR files, copilot doesn't break in. It walks through the front door you left open.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains that Copilot data leakage comes from existing oversharing, not from Copilot itself.

quotes.text: Copilot entropy grows by default. Determinism only exists by design. You own the boundaries or you don't. You own refusal or you don't.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis about architectural responsibility.

quotes.text: Remember, co-pilot didn't assert authority. You granted it by omission. In a distributed decision engine, anything that sounds like policy becomes policy, unless you enforce what policy is.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Pinpoints hallucinated authority as a design gap rather than a model flaw.

quotes.text: The invoice is the only honest stakeholder you have in an unobserved system. It tells you where entropy won.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable framing of cost spikes as a governance signal.

takeaways: Copilot inherits your permissions and oversharing through Microsoft Graph, so default-deny scopes and enforced sensitivity labels are the only real boundaries.
Separate reasoning from execution with the reason, plan, gate, execute pattern, demanding structured plans, citations and rollback before any change runs.
Treat identity, explicit session state, observability and budgets as controls, with dedicated agent identities, least privilege and drift alerts.
hook: Copilot is not a helpful feature layer but a decision engine on top of Microsoft Graph that amplifies every gap in your permissions and governance. This masterclass gives security, legal and IT leaders ten enforceable design mandates, a reusable reason-plan-gate-execute pattern and a red flag test to prevent data leakage, confident fiction and irreversible automation in Microsoft 365.
